findings.evidence: Mathlib always puts the conclusion before `of`: Algebra/Polynomial/Degree/Operations.lean:85 `coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt`, Derivative.lean:699 `iterate_derivative_eq_zero_of_degree_lt`, FieldTheory/Relrank.lean:63 `relrank_eq_rank_of_le`.
findings.issue: `derivativeSign_of_lt` (concl. `= 0`) and `derivativeSign_of_le` (line 122, concl. `derivativeSign p a k = derivativeSign p b k`) carry no conclusion in the name and do not say what the `<`/`≤` compares; as a pair they falsely suggest lt/le variants of one statement.

findings.evidence: Line 186-187 `(hx : x ∈ Icc a b) (h : derivativeSign p a = derivativeSign p b) : derivativeSign p x = derivativeSign p a`; conventions: the name describes the conclusion, `of` separates described hypotheses.
findings.issue: `derivativeSign_between` names only the hypothesis shape (`x ∈ Icc a b`); the conclusion is the equality `derivativeSign p x = derivativeSign p a`, which the name does not state.

findings.evidence: Lines 132-133: `(hne : thomEncoding p a i ≠ thomEncoding p b i) : i.val + 1 < p.natDegree`.
findings.fix: Name it after the conclusion with the hypothesis after `of`, e.g. `succ_lt_natDegree_of_thomEncoding_ne`.
findings.issue: `thomEncoding_lt_natDegree` reads as `thomEncoding … < p.natDegree` (a type error: `SignType` vs `ℕ`). The conclusion is `i.val + 1 < p.natDegree`; `thomEncoding` occurs only in the hypothesis.

findings.evidence: Mathlib names preimage instances with `preimage`: Order/Interval/Set/OrdConnected.lean:208 `ordConnected_preimage`, Algebra/Order/Ring/StandardPart.lean:130 `ordConnected_preimage_mk'`.
findings.issue: `ordConnected_derivativeSign` names the function, but the ord-connected object is the preimage `derivativeSign p ⁻¹' {σ}`.

findings.evidence: Lines 316 and 330 state the same fact for the two encodings; Mathlib spells `+ 1` as `succ`.
findings.issue: `thomEncoding_next_ne_zero` uses the ad-hoc `next` for the `i+1` coordinate, while its twin at line 316 is `derivativeSign_succ_ne_zero`; the other twin pairs (`lt_iff_derivativeSign`/`lt_iff_thomEncoding`, `exists_derivativeSign_ne`/`exists_thomEncoding_ne`) match exactly.

summary: Several public names describe only their hypotheses instead of their conclusions (`derivativeSign_of_lt`, `derivativeSign_of_le`, `derivativeSign_between`), and two name a subject that is not the subject of the statement (`thomEncoding_lt_natDegree`, `ordConnected_derivativeSign`). One twin pair is also inconsistent (`succ` vs `next`).
